observations: Opened assets/panels/06-3.png. A soft pale-blue cloud-shaped vignette surrounds a living-room sofa scene. At left, small clinic silhouettes are linked by dotted lines. There is no text anywhere. The vignette is an oval cloud shape rather than the rounded rectangle used in 06-2, but it still reads as the same vision treatment.
Ravi is on the left: same face, beard, side part and green shirt as the sheet. He looks at the tablet and smiles.

Ravi's right hand, as requested: his arm hangs from his right shoulder (viewer-left), the forearm comes up across his body, and the index finger points at the tablet's top-left corner. Confirmed as his right hand pointing at the tablet.

Ravi's left arm passes behind the partner's hair at shoulder height and comes out at far right. The left hand, which has the wristwatch, rests on the sofa back above and behind the child's shoulder. So it reaches behind both the partner and the child, not only 'behind his partner' as recorded. The reach looks long but possible.

The partner matches vision-cast.png: shoulder-length wavy hair, mustard block-print kurta, small hoop earrings, mole under her right eye (viewer-left). She holds the tablet in both hands at its bottom corners, right hand on the viewer-left corner and left hand on the viewer-right corner. The tablet shows three profile circles and a heart, with no text.
The child matches vision-cast.png: short dark hair, big round eyes, orange T-shirt, khaki shorts. He leans in from the right, smiling at the tablet.

issues.problem: The child's hands do not clearly match production.hands.child. Two hands are visible and both are on the viewer-left side of his body, next to the partner. One rests on her upper arm at shoulder height (around panel x 1150-1200, y 340-390). The other rests low on the cushion at the bottom edge (around x 1210-1250, y 490-515). He is turned three-quarters to screen-left, so the hand on the partner's arm most naturally belongs to his right arm, the near one. The record says left hand on the partner's arm and right hand on the cushion. With both hands on the same side, one arm must cross his body, and I could not trace that arm's path at the size I viewed. Check at 200% which arm each hand belongs to and whether the arms connect properly. Then either correct the record or fix the art. Also make the Ravi left-hand entry say the hand rests on the sofa back behind the child.
